routing_warnings.description: The client requests a plan covering guest posts rather than commissioning guest-post delivery.
This message defines the requested plan's contents, not an agreed guest-post delivery obligation.
This message limits the SEO plan to four service areas but does not independently commission guest-post delivery.
The agency claims delivery of the revised plan, not completion of guest-posting work.
This message specifies keywords to use in blog content rather than changing the campaign keyword-research report.
The requested document concerns blog topics and their associated keywords rather than the campaign keyword-research report.
This repeated request concerns the blog-topic and keyword document rather than the campaign keyword-research report.
This message reports that blogs are live on the website, which concerns publication rather than article drafting and review delivery.
This message reports that the sixth blog was updated on the website.
This message reports that the seventh blog was updated on the website.
This message reports that the eighth blog was updated on the website.
This message reports that the ninth blog was updated on the website.
This requests search-volume data in the keyword report rather than changing the keywords used in blog content.
This claims that keyword and search-volume data were added to the report, not that the selected keywords were used in blogs.
This completion claim concerns changes reflected in the keyword sheet and does not establish use of those keywords in blog articles.
This reports delivery of the final keyword sheet rather than implementation of blog keyword targeting.
The observed omission concerns search-volume data in the keyword sheet.
This claims that keyword-volume information was added to the sheet.
This requests a combined blog-topic and keyword document rather than changing the keyword set to be used in blog content.
This repeats the request for a blog-topic and keyword document without changing blog keyword targeting.
This message requests indexed-link counts and indexing-tool information rather than changing the backlink campaign quantity or link-type ratio.
The observed indexed and unindexed link results and requested remediation concern backlink indexing rather than initial backlink campaign creation.
This implementation claim specifically reports completion of index submission.
The client requests a document showing before-and-after metadata values; this introduces the comparison-report deliverable rather than changing the metadata-optimization Requirement.
The freelancer reports that the before-and-after work report is ready, which is an implementation claim for the comparison-report deliverable.
The requested revised blog theme concerns blog-topic selection rather than general webpage-content optimization.
The implemented suggested changes concern the independently tracked Campus Launch sale page.
The request to replace an item with the Campus Launch sale page occurs in the keyword-report exchange and does not itself establish optimization of that page.
This message changes the intended audience for the AI dolls blog and belongs to the separate audience-targeting Requirement.
The request for the current Google-indexed backlink count is primarily a requirement for an index-status report.
This message requests the outstanding indexing-status update rather than changing the indexing-remediation behavior.
The claim that the index-status report is ready belongs to the separate report Requirement.
The question about replacing links that remain unindexed concerns the separate replacement-policy Requirement.
The instruction to submit all 164 unindexed links through an indexer belongs to the backlink index-submission and remediation Requirement.
The question about replacing links that remain unindexed belongs to the independent replacement-policy Requirement.
